description: Deep-dive platform stability for declarative-conversion-operator: conversion throughput and failure rate, the same webhook/manager series as Conversion Overview, registry readiness, and kubelet/kube-state-metrics resource usage of webhook-server and manager pods.

panels.title: Objects /s
panels.description: Individual objects converted inside ConversionReviews (not reviews). This is the conversion throughput SLI.

panels.title: Reviews /s
panels.description: apiserver ConversionReview RPCs. A review may contain many objects (List/watch conversion).

panels.title: Failure rate
panels.description: Share of ConversionReviews whose result is not success (error, bad_request, not_registered, panic). Chart alert ConversionWebhookErrorRatio fires at result=error >5% per target; this panel is fleet-wide across all non-success results.

panels.title: Error ratio (alert)
panels.description: Fleet-wide result=error ratio — same result filter as alert ConversionWebhookErrorRatio (threshold 5% per target).

panels.title: Review p99
panels.description: End-to-end ConversionReview latency p99. Alert ConversionWebhookHighLatency fires above 1s per target.

panels.title: Ready replicas
panels.description: Webhook replicas whose registry finished initial sync (dco_webhook_ready=1). Alert ConversionWebhookNotReady fires when none are ready.

panels.title: Review p50
panels.description: Median ConversionReview latency. Compare with p99 to spot tail latency.

panels.title: Lossy /s
panels.description: Conversions on a direction statically marked lossy. Alert ConversionWebhookLossyRate fires above 0.01/s per target+direction.

panels.title: Compile errors (15m)
panels.description: Compile failures that left a stale or absent plan. Alert ConversionWebhookRegistryCompileErrors fires on any increase over 15m.

panels.title: Registry size
panels.description: Max compiled-or-placeholder registry entries across scraped webhook replicas (includes error-only placeholders).

panels.title: Stale/Failed (15m)
panels.description: Config phase transitions into Stale (KeepServingStale) or Failed (typically FailClosed revert). Matches alert ManagerPhaseStaleOrFailClosed.

panels.title: Watch-map errors (15m)
panels.description: Secondary watch map List failures. Transient misses recover via RequeueAfter; a sustained rise means the manager cannot see related configs.

panels.title: Per-target conversion SLIs
panels.description: Instant fleet snapshot by XRD/CRD name. Error ratio red at 5% (alert threshold); p99 red at 1s. Open Conversion Target Detail for a single target.

panels.title: Objects converted /s by target and result
panels.description: Object-level throughput. result=success is healthy traffic; anything else is dropped or failed conversion of an object inside a review.

panels.title: Reviews /s by result
panels.description: ConversionReview RPC rate stacked by result: success, error, bad_request, not_registered, panic. Panic should stay at zero.

panels.title: Objects /s by from → to version
panels.description: Spoke/hub version pair traffic. Sudden new pairs usually mean a schema promotion or a client still on an old version.

panels.title: Objects per review (batch size)
panels.description: Mean objects inside each ConversionReview. List/watch conversion drives this up; Get stays near 1. High batch size plus high p99 often means a large List hitting the webhook.

panels.title: Review latency p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Fleet-wide ConversionReview latency percentiles. Webhook is on the apiserver critical path — sustained p99 above ~100ms is worth investigating; 1s matches the chart alert.

panels.title: Review p99 by target
panels.description: Same query as Conversion Overview. Isolate which XRD/CRD is on the tail.

panels.title: Review p99 by direction
panels.description: direction is a version pair (e.g. v1→v3). Hub-bound vs spoke-bound paths can differ when CEL/JSONPatch is one-way.

panels.title: Review latency heatmap
panels.description: Distribution over histogram buckets (100µs … 5s). A mass shifting right is saturation even if p99 has not crossed 1s yet.

panels.title: Failure rate by target
panels.description: Non-success review ratio per target. Alert ConversionWebhookErrorRatio uses result=error only at 5%.

panels.title: Non-success reviews /s by target and result
panels.description: Absolute failure QPS. not_registered means the replica has no compiled plan; panic is a process bug; bad_request is a malformed ConversionReview.

panels.title: Compile errors /s by target and reason
panels.description: Reasons include XRDNotFound, CRDNotFound, InvalidRules, AnalyzeFailed, ValidationErrors. Serving may continue on a stale plan.

panels.title: Lossy conversions /s
panels.description: Known-lossy directions (CEL always-lossy, irreversible maps). Unexpected rate means clients converting the wrong way after a promote.

panels.title: Ready replicas missing a loaded plan
panels.description: A ready replica with no loaded plans cannot convert anything (not_registered). Per-target gaps: (ready==1) unless on(pod) (entry_loaded{target=X}==1).

panels.title: Webhook ready by pod
panels.description: 1 after initial registry sync. 0 for 5m trips ConversionWebhookReplicaNotReady. New pods should flip to 1 quickly after cache sync.

panels.title: Registry size by pod
panels.description: Entries including error-only placeholders. Divergence across replicas means an informer lag or cacheSelector mismatch.

panels.title: Registry reloads /s
panels.description: Compile attempts. A storm of reloads usually means the config or XRD/CRD schema is thrashing.

panels.title: Registry entry loaded (1=servable plan)
panels.description: Per replica × target. 0 is an error-only placeholder — that replica will return not_registered for the target.

panels.title: Seconds since last successful compile
panels.description: Age of the serving plan. Large age is normal when configs are stable; a jump to zero is a reload.

panels.title: Manager analyze failures /s

targets.expr: sum by (config_kind, target, reason) (rate(dco_manager_analyze_failures_total[5m])) or vector(0)

panels.description: Analyze/compile validation failures during config reconcile. Matches alert ManagerReconcileAnalyzeFailures.

panels.title: Manager apply latency p50 / p99
panels.description: SSA patch applying conversion webhook config onto the XRD/CRD. Slow apply delays schema promotions, not live ConversionReviews.

panels.title: Phase transitions /s

targets.expr: sum by (config_kind, from_phase, to_phase, reason) (rate(dco_manager_phase_transitions_total[5m])) or vector(0)

panels.description: Applied→Stale is KeepServingStale after drift; Applied→Failed is typically FailClosed revert. Pending→Applied is healthy first apply.

panels.title: Watch-map List errors /s
panels.description: Watch-mapping List failures (API timeout, etc.). Configs still self-reconcile; a sustained rate means secondary watches are blind.

panels.title: Manager reconcile rate
panels.description: controller-runtime reconcile counters on manager pods. result=error should stay near zero. Series come from the manager scrape, not the webhook dedicated registry.

panels.title: Manager workqueue depth
panels.description: Workqueue backlog on the manager. A climbing depth means reconcile cannot keep up (apiserver latency or a hot loop).

panels.title: Webhook CPU vs request / limit
panels.description: container=webhook-server (operator-owned name). Usage from kubelet cAdvisor; request/limit from kube-state-metrics. ConversionReviews are CPU-bound on CEL/JSONPatch paths — saturation here raises p99.

panels.title: Webhook memory working set vs request / limit
panels.description: Working set for webhook-server. Registry of compiled plans plus ConversionReview payloads. Growth without traffic usually means a leak; OOMKill shows up as a restart spike.

panels.title: Webhook CPU as fraction of request

targets.expr: (sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container="webhook-server", namespace=~"$namespace"}[5m]))) / clamp_min(sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{container="webhook-server", resource="cpu", namespace=~"$namespace"}), 1e-9)

panels.description: >1 means usage above request (throttling risk if a limit is set, or noisy-neighbor if not). HPA on CPU uses this ratio.

panels.title: Webhook memory as fraction of request

targets.expr: (sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{container="webhook-server", namespace=~"$namespace"})) / clamp_min(sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{container="webhook-server", resource="memory", namespace=~"$namespace"}), 1e-9)

panels.description: Working set / request. Approaching 1 with a memory limit is OOM risk.

panels.title: Webhook container restarts (1h)
panels.description: Restarts of webhook-server. Correlate with OOM, liveness failures, or cert/TLS crashes. Each restart drops in-memory registry until InitialSync completes (ready=0).

panels.title: Webhook CPU CFS throttle
panels.description: Seconds spent throttled by CFS. Non-zero with high p99 means the CPU limit is too low for conversion load.

panels.title: Webhook pod network

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(container_network_receive_bytes_total{namespace=~"$namespace"}[5m]) and on(namespace, pod) kube_pod_container_info{container="webhook-server", namespace=~"$namespace"})
sum by (pod) (rate(container_network_transmit_bytes_total{namespace=~"$namespace"}[5m]) and on(namespace, pod) kube_pod_container_info{container="webhook-server", namespace=~"$namespace"})

panels.description: Pod-level network (cAdvisor network series are not on the app container). ConversionReviews are small JSON; a tx spike with object rate is expected.

panels.title: Webhook HPA replicas
panels.description: Empty unless conversionWebhookServer.autoscaling is enabled. Current vs desired lag means the HPA cannot scale (pending pods or maxReplicas).

panels.title: Manager CPU vs request / limit
panels.description: container=manager. Manager is not on the ConversionReview path; CPU here is reconcile/SSA/watch. Saturation delays config apply and phase updates, not live conversions.

panels.title: Manager memory working set vs request / limit
panels.description: Manager working set. Growth with XRD/CRD count is expected (informers). Leader-election standby replicas should be flatter.

panels.title: Manager CPU as fraction of request

targets.expr: (sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container="manager", namespace=~"$namespace"}[5m]))) / clamp_min(sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{container="manager", resource="cpu", namespace=~"$namespace"}), 1e-9)

panels.title: Manager memory as fraction of request

targets.expr: (sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{container="manager", namespace=~"$namespace"})) / clamp_min(sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{container="manager", resource="memory", namespace=~"$namespace"}), 1e-9)

panels.title: Manager container restarts (1h)
panels.description: Manager restarts drop leadership and pause apply until the new leader is elected. Live conversion continues on webhook pods.

panels.title: Manager goroutines
panels.description: Go runtime goroutines from the manager process scrape (webhook /metrics is a dedicated registry without Go collectors). A monotonic climb is a leak.

panels.title: Manager RSS
panels.description: Process RSS from the manager scrape. Compare with cAdvisor working set above; a large gap can be mapped files or Go heap vs container working set.

panels.title: Manager process CPU
panels.description: Process CPU from the manager scrape (user+system). Should track cAdvisor usage.

title: Conversion Platform Stability
